indicators.note: the word left sits inside the newly-wed, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a newly-wed woman is a bride

explanation.surface: A newly married woman is said to have been left in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridle is the headgear and reins used to steer and restrain a horse, so it serves as a means of restraint.

clue.text: Having lost one's shirt on a horse!

definitions.text: Having lost one's shirt on a horse!

parts.words: Having lost one's shirt on a horse!
parts.note: seems to describe a gambler ruined by a bet, but literally means riding with an uncovered torso and no saddle

explanation.surface: A punter has lost everything on a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Riding without a saddle on the animal's bare body is the style meant; lost shirt also suggests a naked torso.

clue.text: Famous, but wrong about Tory leader

indicators.note: the word for wrong is placed about the Tory leader, enclosing it

parts.note: immoral means morally wrong

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A celebrity is criticised for being wrong about the head of the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party.
explanation.definitionFit: An immortal is someone whose fame lives forever, so the adjective means everlastingly famous.

parts.note: to linger is to stay on
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A request to stay, which is to say, a corset is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: Stays are an old word for a corset, hence 'perhaps' signalling an example of women's underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsets, once called stays, are an example of women's underwear.

definitions.meaning: a sturdy framework of poles and boards put up around a building
the platform on which condemned people were hanged or beheaded

explanation.surface: Someone voices firm backing for the death penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Builders erect a framework of poles round a building, and the gallows platform for executions carries the same name.

parts.note: curt means short or brusque
ailing means unwell, off colour

explanation.surface: Someone halts abruptly because they feel unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtailing means cutting short, bringing something to a stop early.

indicators.note: the publicity goes in the countenance, inside it

parts.note: a countenance is a face
an ad is publicity, an advertisement

explanation.surface: A face appears in an advert in a shop window.
explanation.definitionFit: A façade is the outward front of a building, such as a shopfront.

clue.text: Beginnings of religion in Genesis is now beginning

indicators.note: the beginning of each of these words is its first letter

explanation.surface: Genesis is where the origins of religion begin.
explanation.definitionFit: Origin means starting point or source, so it stands for beginnings.

parts.note: a crook is a bend, as is an angle

explanation.surface: A dishonest Democrat politician is to be suspended.
explanation.definitionFit: To dangle is to hang loosely, so it means to suspend.

clue.text: Found in harem in Dubai, nudge!

indicators.note: the letters are found running inside the words harem in Dubai

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style exclamation about something discovered in a sultan's harem.
explanation.definitionFit: To nudge someone is to jog their memory, prompting them about something.

indicators.note: the lie wraps around the right, so it goes about it

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An argument arises over whether a claim of entitlement is false.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is conflict or disagreement between people, a synonym for dispute.

indicators.note: in an across answer the control piece is placed on, that is after, the British piece

parts.note: order means control, as in keeping order

explanation.surface: Passport checks are imposed at Britain's frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A border is the boundary line between countries, i.e. a frontier.

parts.note: to hand something is to give it
Bill Clinton, US president

explanation.surface: Someone is told to serve the former president with a formal warning.
explanation.definitionFit: A handbill is a printed leaflet distributed by hand, a public notice or flyer.

indicators.note: irregular means out of order, so the letters of saw nothing are rearranged

explanation.surface: A one-time head of state claims to have witnessed nothing untoward.
explanation.definitionFit: George Washington was the first president of the USA.

clue.text: Good daily fare protects his heart

indicators.note: the daily and fare pieces enclose the heart of his, protecting it

parts.note: a daily is a cleaning lady, a char
table means the food served, as in keeping a good table

indicators.note: the heart of the word his is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A healthy everyday diet looks after a man's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' is British slang for a cleaner who comes in each day, also called a char.
explanation.definitionFit: A charitable person is kind and generous, which is what good means here.

indicators.note: possibly suggests another arrangement, so the letters of some limb are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clot may have formed in some arm or leg.
explanation.definitionFit: An embolism is the obstruction of an artery by a clot or air bubble.

indicators.note: errant means wandering astray, so the letters of the fodder are moved about

parts.note: the setter evidently meant the words on traces here; the printed son is a slip for on

explanation.surface: A wayward son tracks down a family member.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed fodder has one S too many; the anagram works only with ONTRACES.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor is a forebear, a kind of family member.

parts.note: to flatter is to praise excessively

indicators.note: the concluding letter of fatuity is taken

explanation.surface: Compliments that end up as hollow foolishness.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattery is excessive, insincere compliment that amounts to hollow foolishness.

clue.text: Stunning bird with old blokes? They're in mate!

indicators.note: the bird, old and blokes pieces go inside the word for mate

parts.note: a pal is a friend, a mate
a hen is a female bird
blokes are men

explanation.surface: A striking woman out with some old men, all of them friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomenal means extraordinary or remarkable, which is how stunning is used of a sight or performance.

clue.text: Taken into custody by bench, say

indicators.note: say signals that the word sounds like another

parts.note: the bench is the judges, so a court of law

explanation.surface: A suspect is arrested and taken before the magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech COURT and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone caught has been seized by the police, i.e. arrested.

parts.note: sounds like a lucrative investment, but bucks are the leaps of an untamed horse

explanation.surface: A tip for something that could earn a lot of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild horse of the American West is known for bucking hard to throw riders.

annotationWithheld.why: Radio operator's station on board (6): the only parse is PARK inside SS, with 'on board' both supplying SS and signalling the container

clue.text: Drug for transplant operation lacking oxygen

indicators.note: transplant suggests moving material elsewhere, so the remaining letters are rearranged
lacking means one letter of operation goes missing

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An anaesthetic is needed for organ surgery done without an oxygen supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' drops an O (oxygen) from OPERATION to leave PERATION, and 'transplant' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Atropine is a poisonous alkaloid from deadly nightshade, used medicinally, so it is a drug.

indicators.note: the forecast goes in between the letters for financial times

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
an omen is a forecast or portent

explanation.surface: A quick economic prediction appears in the pink business paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a British business newspaper, known as the FT.
explanation.definitionFit: To foment is to stir up or instigate trouble, so it means to prompt, used as a verb.

indicators.note: an unruly thing is disorderly, so the letters of teenager are disordered

explanation.surface: A dad's son is a difficult adolescent.
explanation.definitionFit: To father something is to bring it into being, to create or produce it.

clue.text: Not much in bed, the French take time

parts.note: lit is the French word for a bed, so being in bed gives lit
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Someone in bed takes a short break before the French lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: Little as a quantity means a small amount, hardly any.

indicators.note: free means let loose, so the letters of handouts are set loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Lots of complimentary gifts are on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: A number in the thousands is a large quantity, so the word stands for a great many.

parts.note: SM is the abbreviation for sergeant-major
troops form an army

explanation.surface: A smooth sergeant-major commands his soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarmy means ingratiating and oily in manner, slick in the unpleasant sense.
